title: Malta Year 8 Math Chapter 2 — Number Work Recap
question: Can you round, follow BIDMAS, find primes, the HCF and the LCM, and work out squares, cubes and roots?
intro: **Quick recap:** round by the next digit; BIDMAS — brackets, powers, \(\times\div\), then \(+-\); a prime has exactly two factors; HCF is the biggest shared factor, LCM the smallest shared multiple.

questions.title: 2.1 · Nearest 100
questions.solution:
The digit after the hundreds is 8, so round up:

\[4\,386 \approx \boxed{4\,400}\]

\(4\,300\) rounds down, but 8 is 5 or more.

questions.title: 2.1 · One decimal place
questions.solution:
The digit after the tenths is 6, so round up:

\[7.462 \approx \boxed{7.5}\]

\(7.4\) does not check the next digit.

questions.title: 2.1 · Value of a digit
questions.prompt: What is the value of the 6 in \(36\,405\)?
questions.solution:
\[36\,405 = 30\,000 + \boxed{6\,000} + 400 + 5\]

\(60\,000\) uses the ten-thousands place, where the 3 sits.

questions.title: 2.2 · Multiply before adding
questions.solution:
\[8 + 4\times3 = 8 + 12 = \boxed{20}\]

\(36\) adds first, as if it were \((8 + 4)\times3\).

questions.title: 2.2 · Powers first
questions.solution:
Power, then multiply, then subtract:

\[50 - 9\times4 = 50 - 36 = \boxed{14}\]

\(26\) uses \(3\times2 = 6\) instead of \(3^2 = 9\).

questions.title: 2.3 · Prime number
questions.solution:
\[\boxed{31} = 1\times31 \text{ only}\]

\(21 = 3\times7\), \(27 = 3\times9\) and \(33 = 3\times11\): odd numbers are not always prime.

questions.title: 2.3 · Prime factors
questions.prompt: Which shows \(60\) as a product of **prime** factors?
questions.solution:
\[60 = 2\times30 = 2\times2\times15 = \boxed{2^2\times3\times5}\]

The others also make 60, but 30, 10, 4 and 15 are not prime.

questions.title: 2.4 · HCF
questions.solution:
Factors of 16: 1, 2, 4, **8**, 16. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, **8**, 12, 24.

\[\text{HCF} = \boxed{8}\]

\(4\) is a common factor, but not the highest one.

questions.title: 2.4 · LCM
questions.solution:
Multiples of 6: 6, 12, **18**. Multiples of 9: 9, **18**.

\[\text{LCM} = \boxed{18}\]

\(54 = 6\times9\) is a common multiple, but not the lowest.

questions.title: 2.5 · Square root
questions.solution:
\(9\times9 = 81\):

\[\sqrt{81} = \boxed{9}\]

\(40.5\) halves 81 — a square root is not a half.

questions.title: 2.5 · Cube root
questions.solution:
\(4\times4\times4 = 64\):

\[\sqrt[3]{64} = \boxed{4}\]

\(8\) is the square root of 64, not the cube root.

takeaway: Round by the next digit, follow BIDMAS, build every number from primes, use the HCF for the biggest equal share and the LCM for the next time things meet, and undo a power with its root.
